page: OVHcloud i1-180 is a storage-optimized virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Haswell architecture CPU clocked at 2.2 GHz, configured with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without multithreading (1 thread per core). Memory capacity is 180.0 GB, providing approximately 5.62 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 7,650 GB of local NVMe SSD storage (configured as 7,600 GB NVMe combined with 50 GB SSD) and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It operates without discrete GPUs and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core execution reflects older microarchitecture constraints, scoring in the bottom percentiles on Geekbench single-core (931.0), single-threaded gzip compression (18.82 GB/sec), and bzip3 decompression (7.33 GB/sec). However, multi-core scaling reaches the middle 50% across most standard evaluations, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,360.0, a PassMark CPU score of 26,126.12, and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 29,468.02. Memory bandwidth reaches 75.8 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 31.69 GB/sec for uncached write operations.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the i1-180 is its heavy reliance on aggregated multi-core parallelism to offset modest single-thread efficiency. Advanced vector instruction support is limited to AVX and FMA, lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. In application-focused tests, it achieves stable average results for static web serving throughput (15.65 GB/sec), PassMark database operations (12,923.35), and Redis SET operations (28.72 million operations/sec), while token generation for LLM inference falls into the bottom percentiles.

Given its massive 7,650 GB local NVMe SSD storage and 180 GB memory footprint paired with 32 dedicated cores, the instance is cost-effective for I/O-intensive storage pools and distributed databases rather than raw compute pipelines. It is suited for large database clusters, distributed search indices, intermediate ETL data stages, and log aggregation platforms requiring dense, high-speed local disk capacity.
description: OVHcloud i1-180 is a storage-optimized instance running on KVM, featuring 32 dedicated x86_64 Intel Haswell cores at 2.2 GHz, 180.0 GB of RAM, and 7,650 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It provides an 8 Gbps baseline network throughput without dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations show weak single-core performance, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 931.0 and single-thread compression bottlenecks, but consistent median results across multi-threaded tests, including a 26,126.12 PassMark CPU score and 28.72 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 75.8 GB/sec for large uncached reads. The server trades per-core execution speed for substantial high-speed disk volume and high memory density. This profile fits I/O-heavy workloads, including large database hosting, search indexing, and distributed data processing that benefit from dense local NVMe storage.
